findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:13,22,29 requires requiredCommands to be part of the pack and its default covered refs, but verification_context_pack_create never accepts requiredCommands (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:295-308, packages/main/src/handlers/verification-context-pack.ts:10-23) and allContextPackRequiredRefs ignores pack.requiredCommands entirely (packages/main/src/core/authority-contracts.ts:257-269). In this state the CLI slice cannot express or mechanically enforce required-command coverage, so the authority protocol is still incomplete.

docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:15 says verifiers can request controlled context-pack expansions, and the core expansion type supports impactedSymbols/dependencyEdges/sourceSnippets (packages/main/src/core/verification-context-pack.ts:38-47,300-320). But the public CLI command and handler only expose impactedFiles/requiredRefs/tokenBudget/metadata (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:310-317, packages/main/src/handlers/verification-context-pack.ts:42-49). That means expansion requests cannot actually carry the additional symbol/snippet/dependency context the design calls for, so the user-facing expansion flow is only partially implemented.

docs/requirements/NAV.md:3-16 is still inaccurate after this update. The generator contract in packages/main/src/tasks/truth.ts writes NAV from all docs/requirements/**/*.md files and uses repo-relative forward-slash links, but the checked-in file claims only 10 files, omits multiple existing decision docs (for example cc-learnings, role-separation, session-ownership-and-write-leases, stack-layering), and keeps backslash links. That leaves the touchpoint users were told to trust out of sync with the actual truth-source set.

docs/requirements/decisions/verification-context-pack.md:15 and :31 present Python-side limits/presets as settled contract (maxContextPackExpansionDepth, maxContextPackEstimatedTokens, anti-hallucination, strict-ci), but those identifiers do not exist anywhere else in this repo. For a truth-source document whose job is to guide future CLI/Runner/Python sync, these need either a cited upstream authority or wording that clearly marks them as proposed external expectations rather than established current behavior.
